title: Fix the Overflowing String Copy
description: The program should safely combine a name into a fixed-size greeting buffer.
expectedBehavior: The program should safely produce a greeting without corrupting memory, even for a long name.
actualProblem: greeting only has 10 bytes total, already partly used by "Hi ". Appending the 10-character name "Alexandria" plus its terminator needs far more space than remains, so strcat writes well past the end of the buffer — a serious buffer overflow.
explanation: Buffers used with strcat must be large enough to hold the combined result, including the null terminator. Using strncat with an explicit remaining-space limit (and sizing the buffer generously) prevents writing past the buffer's end.
